content.v: Do you love capybaras? Many do. These web-footed

of the moment. They have millions of fans worldwide. Now, capybara lovers in St. Augustine, Florida, have a great place to visit. At the Capybara Café, they can feed and pet these animals, and might even have one climb into their lap.
Since its opening in October 2024, the café has welcomed hundreds of animal lovers. Leah Macri is a regular visitor. “Their fur kind of feels like
,” she said. “When they get comfortable enough, they’ll fall over.”

There is a daily limit to the number of visitors. Entries must be booked several months ahead. After entering the café, visitors are taken into a smaller room in groups of six. They are given blankets to place over their lap. Then, three capybaras are brought into the room for the humans to interact with. The 30-minute experience costs $49 per person. Although it’s called a café, the place doesn’t sell coffee. It only sells capybara-themed T-shirts, cups, and stuffed animals. The income supports a local

Following owls, foxes, and sloths, capybaras are the latest animals to receive star treatment. Over the past few years, capybara-themed slippers, purses, and notebooks have filled gift shops. Some zoos and wildlife parks now let visitors pet these
animals. But Macri said that none of them allows for the same close connection with the animals as the Capybara Café does.

Stephanie Angel, the café’s owner, plans to open another capybara café. The new place will also be in Florida. But considering the animals’ popularity, perhaps many other cities will see similar “cafés” soon.
